transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for grades 6 through 8, and I've asked each of you here because I need your input before I can approve it. The draft plan currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear any concerns or recommendations each of you has regarding these elements. Let's start with you — what should I know from your area of expertise before I sign off on this?

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I need to flag a staffing concern. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it contains 18 student tutors. The school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. That means we'd need at least three adult supervisors, not two as the draft plan currently states. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two supervisors, so that needs to be updated before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I have a critical concern regarding the student-selected tutor pairings. This week I completed a student-support review, and it identified two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. These restrictions are currently recorded only in confidential counseling files, so no one else at this table would have been aware of them. Because of this, tutor pairings cannot be left to student selection — they must be assigned and monitored by me, as the counselor, to ensure we don't inadvertently place students in sessions with someone they have a no-contact restriction against. This is a student safety issue that needs to be addressed before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I have a critical concern regarding the technology platform in the draft plan. Google Classroom is not approved for this program's student-to-student communication. The district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment is the approved platform, and it retains the required school records. I confirmed the platform settings with district IT this week, but the technology field in the draft application has not been updated and still lists Google Classroom. This needs to be corrected to Microsoft Teams before approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I have a concern regarding the consent form process in the draft plan. I confirmed the procedure with the family-engagement office this week, and for this program, family consent must be entered in the student information system before a student participates — not just collected on paper. Additionally, the district has approved translated electronic forms in addition to paper forms, which is important for accessibility across our families. The draft plan still describes only paper collection without any SIS entry, so this needs to be corrected before approval.
